published.answer: 17: A+Z cross (2), A back (1), Omar+Grandad cross (10), Z back (2), A+Z cross (2)

published.title: Two doors, one lion; Person 1 always tells the truth, Person 2 always lies; one question to one guard
published.answer: Ask either guard: 'If I asked the other guard which door leads outside, which door would he point to?' Then take the OTHER door. (Truth-teller reports the liar's lie; liar lies about the truth-teller's answer: both point to the lion door.)

published.title: The broken vase: heavy rain all morning; Person 1 reading in the garden, Person 2 baking in the kitchen, Person 3 asleep upstairs
published.answer: Person 1. It had been raining heavily since sunrise, so nobody could have been reading in the garden the whole time (and the book is perfectly dry).

published.title: Three boxes (apples, oranges, mixed); Person 1 got every label wrong; take one fruit from one box without looking, then fix all three labels
published.answer: Box 3, the one labelled MIXED. Its label is wrong, so it holds only one kind. If you pull an apple, it is the apples box; the box labelled ORANGES can't be oranges (wrong label) and can't be apples, so it's mixed; the box labelled APPLES is oranges. (Same logic the other way round if you pull an orange.)
